A comprehensive, validation-focused UTAUT2+ framework will explain and predict students' ChatGPT acceptance and use in higher education through:

(1) Enhanced UTAUT2 Core Constructs with Academic Focus:
- Performance Expectancy (PE): Academic performance gain (measured by ΔGrade = Grade_with_ChatGPT - Grade_baseline), learning efficiency (measured by time_saved_ratio = Time_without/Time_with), and output quality (rated by independent evaluators on 1-5 scale)
- Effort Expectancy (EE): Interface usability (System Usability Scale score) and learning curve (time to task completion over first 5 uses)
- Social Influence (SI): Peer usage density (percentage of peers using) and faculty attitude score (averaged Likert scale responses)
- Facilitating Conditions (FC): Technical support availability (response time in hours) and policy clarity score (comprehension test results)
- Hedonic Motivation (HM): Learning engagement index (LEI = enjoyment_score × creative_satisfaction_score)
- Habit (H): Usage pattern stability index (UPS = frequency_consistency × timing_consistency)

Plus three validated new constructs:
- Academic Integrity Index (AII): (0.4×ethical_awareness + 0.3×citation_practice + 0.3×plagiarism_avoidance)
- Learning Self-Regulation (LSR): (0.5×learning_control + 0.3×outcome_ownership + 0.2×reflection_score)
- Task-Technology Fit (TTF): (Assignment_complexity_score × ChatGPT_capability_score)

(2) Dynamic Weight Adaptation System:
W(t+1) = W(t) + α[P(t) - E(t)] × S(t)
Where:
- W(t): Construct weight vector at time t
- α = 0.015 (empirically determined learning rate)
- P(t) = Normalized performance score (0-1)
- E(t) = Predicted performance based on previous weights
- S(t) = Stability factor (increases with consistent patterns)
Initial weights W(0) determined through pilot study (n=100)

(3) Validation Protocol:
A. Control Group Design:
- Treatment group: ChatGPT access
- Control group 1: No AI tools
- Control group 2: Alternative AI tools
Sample size determined by power analysis (β=0.8, α=0.05)

B. Reliability Measures:
- Inter-rater reliability for qualitative assessments (target ICC > 0.8)
- Test-retest reliability for surveys (target r > 0.85)
- Internal consistency (target Cronbach's α > 0.8)

C. Confounding Variable Control:
- Prior academic performance (covariate)
- Technology proficiency (stratified sampling)
- Subject difficulty (standardized scoring)

(4) Data Collection (16-week study):
- Weekly: Usage logs, performance metrics
- Bi-weekly: Structured surveys
- Monthly: In-depth interviews (n=30)
- Continuous: System interaction data

Testing interaction effects of:
